subject: Benchmark compendium + MAP deliverables: slides, CSV exports, dashboards
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging plan for ACME MAP: final checklist

Team —

As we move towards the MAP close with ACME next week, I want to lock the packaging deliverables for the performance run we completed on 2027-09-14. The buyer expects a compact compendium they can circulate with execs:

- Single-slide executive summary (p95 latency, TTFT, peak qps, concurrency scaling) — Marissa to own
- Full CSV exports of each run (token-level summaries + per-run metadata) — Evelyn to own
- Grafana dashboard snapshot + a short explainer link for the MAP README — Karthik to own
- A one-paragraph interpretation for legal/procurement to attach to the deck (data-retention/PII notes) — Laura to draft

Acceptance criteria (from MAP):
- p95 and TTFT values annotated with sequence-length contexts (128/512/1024)
- Concurrency curve (1->128 concurrent sessions) with clear hardware callout (8xA100 80GB, CUDA 11.8)
- CSVs include run_id, model_variant, batch_size, qps, p50/p95/p99, ttft_ms, total_tokens

Timeline: target to hand off the full artifact bundle to me by EOD 2027-09-14 so I can route to ACME and schedule the exec readout. If anything blocks, flag it inside 24h.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-13T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging plan for ACME MAP: final checklist

Diego — quick status:

- Executive slide: draft completed. Contains 3 charts (p95 by seq len, concurrency scaling, ttft distribution). I pulled the target p95 numbers from the 2027-09-14 runs: p95@128=18ms, p95@512=45ms, p95@1024=112ms for the tuned fp16 + Q8_0 path.
- Slides saved as ACME_benchmark_deck_20270914.pptx (attached locally).
- Generating speaker notes that map each chart to MAP acceptance language.

Attachments saved to S3 at: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-share/2027-09-14/acme-benchmark-exports.zip (contains CSVs and the deck)

I still need the run-level metadata CSV (Evelyn) to join with my charts so the slide footers can reference run_ids.

-Marissa

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeinfra.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@acmeinfra.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ACME Infra Procurement <procurement@acmeinfra.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T20:05:00-07:00
Subject: ACME performance compendium + MAP artifact bundle (deliverable)

Hi Alice / Michael —

Thanks again for the time this week. Per our MAP milestone (Deliverable: Performance evidence pack), please find the compendium we ran on 2027-09-14. The bundle includes:

- Executive summary slide (ACME_benchmark_deck_20270914.pptx) — top-line metrics and one-slide interpretation for your execs.
- CSV exports (acme_benchmarks_runs_20270914.csv, acme_benchmarks_per_run_metadata.csv) — raw per-run metrics and metadata for audit.
- Grafana snapshot and explainer: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/abcd123/acme-perf-summary
- S3 bundle with all artifacts: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-share/2027-09-14/acme-benchmark-exports.zip

Executive highlights:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) is reported as median=8ms for seq_len=128, median=22ms for seq_len=512, and median=48ms for seq_len=1024 on the tuned fp16 path.
- p95 latency: 18ms (128), 45ms (512), 112ms (1024) under single-session load.
- Sustained throughput peak observed: 22k tokens/sec across the 8xA100 pool at 64 concurrent sessions; concurrency curve attached in slide 2.

Notes on methodology: runs were executed with identical prompt sets used in your eval plan, CPU pinning and CUDA streams set to the values in the readme. All exports include the run_id that maps to the command used to reproduce results.

Next MAP step: schedule a 30-min exec readout to walk the top-line and handoff artifacts to procurement/legal for SOC/audit items. Proposed windows: 2027-09-16 09:00–10:00 PDT or 2027-09-16 15:00–15:30 PDT. If procurement needs separate context, Laura can add the paragraph about data handling.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeinfra.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acmeinfra.com>, ACME Infra Procurement <procurement@acmeinfra.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME performance compendium + MAP artifact bundle (deliverable)

Thanks Diego — the bundle looks thorough, appreciate the quick turnaround. A few quick clarifications before we share with our execs/procurement: 

1) On TTFT: can you confirm the exact measurement point? Is TTFT measured from request send to model first-token on the network, or to Redwood's runtime output queue? We need the number we can put into our latency SLOs.

2) p95 numbers look good — can you attach the per-sequence-length p95 CSV (I see run-level numbers but want the underlying distribution)?

3) Procurement asked whether the CSV exports contain any user prompt text (PII). If so, can you provide a redacted copy or confirm redaction policy?

If we can get a short 15-min call to confirm items 1 and 3 today, we can lock the MAP Acceptance on 2027-09-16.

—Alice
Alice Zhang
Director, Platform Engineering, ACME Infra

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ACME Infra Procurement <procurement@acmeinfra.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME performance compendium + MAP artifact bundle (deliverable)

Alice — thanks for the quick review, answers below and proposed short sync: 

1) TTFT definition: we report TTFT as time between request arrival at the Redwood public endpoint (post-LB) and the first token emitted by the runtime (i.e., includes network ingress and request serialization, but not external queuing before the LB). We can provide a CSV column ttft_ms_raw (network-timestamped) and ttft_ms_runtime (runtime-side) for your SLO mapping.

2) Per-seq-length distributions: Evelyn exported a per-token distribution CSV and I have a redacted copy ready that removes prompt text. I'll attach acme_benchmarks_per_seqlen_p95_20270914.csv to the package and upload to the same S3 bundle by EOD.

3) PII/redaction: the CSV exports in the shared bundle do NOT contain raw user prompt text; the run metadata includes prompt hashes only. Procurement: Laura will add a one-paragraph confirmation on retention scope and redaction policy in the next e-mail.

Proposed sync: 2027-09-15 15:30–15:45 PDT (15 min) — quick review of TTFT definitions and procurement redaction note. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and attach the redacted CSVs. After the sync we can mark MAP Acceptance and move to contract finalization.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
